rationale: Reproduced from pixels and source. CFP-S3/022 and CFP-S4/006 are the SAME record (sub_synthetic_pool_0002), so the comparison is sound. Mechanism differs from the judge's account: 'maybe' is the review row's own recommendation column, NOT the record lifecycle chip (the sibling row reads 4.20 approve and the record chip reads 'In review'). Root cause: EvaluationPanelResult (SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:217) renders evaluation.comment and evaluation.recommendation (review-row columns) while the reviewer's scorecard Comments text criterion and Recommendation live in criteria_scores; ScorecardAnswers exists but is wired at line 285, not into the panel at line 706. NOT a regression: panel path unchanged since before the baseline (last relevant commit 9fcab246, 2026-08-13). Baseline showed the same fault as an em dash (baseline defect[3], minor) because that record carried no committee note; round 11 shows it as misattribution because the seeded record does.

The graded build already ships submitter-visible outcomes. 57c8379c (#225, 2026-08-14 03:21 EDT) added publicOutcomeForSubmission() and distinct accepted/waitlisted/rejected confirmation copy on the private resume link; 995394c6 (#234) added the decision-lock explanation. Both verified ancestors of the graded sha c9a6e9a51141. The judge captured CFP-S2/012 immediately post-submit, when status is still 'submitted' and the code's default branch returns null, and generalised that to 'no decision surface'. The run never re-loaded the resume link after the CFP-S4 accept/reject, so the shipped capability was never exercised. Residual and NOT patched: no chip for the in-between Submitted/Under-review states, which is a product choice rather than a defect.

Narrow display/timezone fault in the builder's datetime round-trip; stored value is correct, so the blast radius is the read-back only. Adjacent contract 76eb02e7 (#233) already fixes reviewer round close dates as UTC calendar days; the builder input renders the stored UTC instant into a local datetime-local control, producing exactly the observed +4h EDT shift.
Copy-level: the outbox generates 'We received <title>' and marks it sent, while the banner promises only future follow-up. Smallest honest fix is to say a receipt is on its way.

description: Round 11 ABS-S2 and ABS-S3 DID exercise the invite-reviewer flow (reviewer invited with link, reviewer seat taken via that link), independently confirming the capability is present in the graded build and that CFP-10's move to partial is purely a browse gap.

One review carries two recommendation inputs and two comment inputs: the scorecard's own criteria, and the review row's recommendation/comment columns. They can disagree and did. Which governs (or whether to collapse them) changes product semantics and is the operator's call; PR 243 only stops the panel from hiding one of them.

A fully completed review summarised as empty: 'REVIEWER RATING — · approve / REVIEWER COMMENT —' while the reviewer had stored Originality 4, Relevance 2, Recommendation Accept and a paragraph of comments, which the list view aggregated to a weighted 3.34.

rationale: SAME ROOT CAUSE as eval:2026-08-14T14-46-26:call-for-papers:0, confirmed by reading both judgements and the source: EvaluationPanelResult renders only the review row (score/recommendation/comment) and never criteria_scores. The CFP area saw it as misattribution because that record carried a seeded committee note; this area saw it as emptiness because the optional score and note were genuinely blank. The judge's own parenthetical — that the detail may be reachable in a section further down the record — is exactly right: EvaluationEvidenceRow renders ScorecardAnswers one card lower. No second branch opened.

description: CSV import creates same-name duplicate people (two Marcus Okafor, two Priya Raman) distinguishable only by truncated email/company, with no merge or link-duplicates control.

rationale: The importer's behaviour is CORRECT and should not be 'fixed' quietly: keying on normalized email means two addresses are two people, which is exactly right, and the judge notes the importer states its per-row reasoning honestly. What is missing is a merge path, and person-merge is product semantics with real blast radius here — notes, tags, custom values and participations all hang off person_id, and CLAUDE.md forbids per-event speaker rows, so a merge has to reconcile org-level identity against every event's participation. That is the operator's call, not a triage patch. A narrow display-only disambiguation (untruncated email, or a collision marker when names match) is available separately and does not need the same decision.

The portal reads 'Viewing as speaker · organizer preview' even on a genuine speaker session reached through the speaker's own one-time sign-in link, misdescribing who is signed in.

rationale: Manual 'Add speaker' never exercised because both fixture speakers already existed from earlier areas. Creation with profile fields WAS proven by CSV import (three people with name, email, title, company, bio), and persistence was proven twice over — sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 survived a reload and a fresh session in the next scenario. Judge's own words: 'an evidence gap, not a demonstrated product failure.'
First forward movement of the round; area went 13 pass/2 partial to 14 pass/1 partial, net +1.

NOT A DEFECT, and patching it would have broken a working feature. There are two distinct routes in src/routes/speaker-invites.routes.ts. inviteSpeakers (:86) is the genuine invite — it emails the speaker a magic link and redirects to plain /portal, which renders NO banner. previewSpeakerPortal (:164) is a separate ops-only route whose own description reads 'Mints a one-time organizer-only portal link without notifying the speaker or changing conference status', guarded by authHasRole(auth,'ops'), and it deliberately redirects to /portal?viewing_as=speaker. The banner is gated on exactly that parameter, so it appears only on a session created by an organizer preview mint. The run reached the portal through the preview link, so the banner was telling the truth about the link's provenance; the organizer having signed out first does not change where the link came from. Contract source: MRQ-153, asserted by tests/integration/api/speaker-files.MRQ-138.test.ts:203 and tests/unit/submitter-portal.MRQ-150.test.ts:229.
